typical_symptoms: Downward cupping and curling of leaf edges (hopperburn)
Reddening and bronzing of leaf borders under prolonged attack
Stunted plant growth and premature leaf drop
Nymphs and adults feeding on leaf undersides and petioles
visual_characteristics: Small, pale-green to yellowish wedge-shaped insects on leaf veins or petioles
Chlorotic leaf borders progressing inward toward primary veins
Downward leaf curling producing a distinctive inverted-cup shape
Marginal leaf tissue necrosis turning reddish-brown to dry brown
color_characteristics: Initial pale yellow at leaf margins progressing to bright yellow, bronze, reddish-brown, and brittle dark brown
spatial_patterns: Marginal distribution spreading inward from leaf edges
Insects scattered along abaxial primary and secondary veins
distinguishing_features: Downward leaf cupping accompanied by marginal reddening and yellowing (hopperburn)
Small pale-green, wedge-shaped jassid nymphs that walk sideways when disturbed
